novelty_status: Concrete Stokes-specific statement established and compared with checked primary sources; no exhaustive novelty certification or claim that general robust transfer is open.

sources.title: On Squared-Variable Formulations
sources.read: PDF Section 3.2, Theorem 3.6, Corollary 3.7, Definitions 3.4-3.5; Section 2 scope checked
sources.html_locators: Theorem 13, Corollary 14; HTML numbering differs from PDF
sources.established: Approximate squared-slack 2N transfers to approximate weak 2N; rank and conditioning dependencies are explicit in its hypotheses.
sources.difference: Our narrower strongly convex Stokes class gives a direct uniform objective-gap bound with explicit constants and one radial lower-curvature test. General quantitative transfer is not novel.

sources.title: Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz Exponent via Hadamard Parametrization
sources.read: PDF Theorem 3.11, Remarks 3.12-3.15; HTML Theorem 17, Remark 18 and surrounding assumptions/proof
sources.established: Local KL exponent (1+beta)/2 under KL and Holderian error-bound assumptions; common convex losses have exponent 3/4 without strict complementarity.
sources.difference: The 4/3 power is a known consequence of a KL 3/4 gradient inequality. Our claim is the uniform explicit Stokes implication with scalar curvature and an error model, not novelty of that exponent.

sources.title: From the simplex to the sphere: Faster constrained optimization using the Hadamard parametrization
sources.established: Qualitative compactness proximity of approximate SOSPs and an algorithmic objective-gap guarantee under strict-saddle, all-local-global and nondegenerate-KKT assumptions.
sources.difference: The stopping theorem is deterministic and does not require an unknown optimal neighborhood or those nondegeneracy assumptions, but assumes strong convexity of the physical objective.

sources.established: Exact criticality transfer and kernel-curvature differential calculus. Historical future-work wording does not establish current open status.
